rows.subtype: Cheek movement in fatigue and stress [Regulating]
rows.description: An adult under stress may clench the cheeks or puff out a breath, signs of tension. Noticing these in oneself can prompt a short break, and in others gentle support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: tiredness, relief from stress

rows.description: A young adult sees raised cheeks with crinkled eyes and reads warmth, but knows some people show pleasure with little cheek movement. Baseline expression differs by person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: affection

rows.description: A young professional tightens or presses the lips to hold back a comment, a sign of restraint. Naming the concern calmly later can be better than swallowing it every time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: calm

rows.subtype: Trembling voice and lips at emotional moments [Regulating]
rows.description: An adult's lips tremble when speaking about something moving, a normal sign of strong feeling. Slow breathing and a pause help, and listeners can be patient.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: relief from stress

rows.description: A colleague juts the jaw in a disagreement, which may signal resolve, defensiveness or fear. Staying calm and asking questions can de-escalate, and leaving is fine if it feels unsafe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear, calm, trust, determination

rows.subtype: Tongue in cheek humour at work [Mismatch]
rows.description: A young professional pairs a tongue-in-cheek face with a dry remark, signalling a joke. With people who do not know them well the humour can be missed, so a smile clarifies.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: amusement
related concepts: humour

rows.subtype: Blank expression in exhaustion or burnout [Interpreting]
rows.description: A colleague with a blank face for weeks may be exhausted, low or overloaded, not uninterested. A private, kind check-in and practical help matter more than judging attitude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: interest, tiredness

rows.description: An adult notices a tense, rigid face before a hard talk and softens it with slow breaths and relaxing the shoulders. A calmer face often makes the conversation easier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: calm, relief from stress

rows.description: A young professional nods regularly to show engagement, which can be reassuring, but constant nodding may hide disagreement. Voicing a concern respectfully is better than nodding through.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, interest

rows.subtype: Bowing the head in respect and mourning [Expressing]
rows.description: An adult bows the head at a funeral, prayer or a formal greeting to show respect or grief. The meaning shifts with setting and tradition, and observers follow local custom.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, grief
